name: Punjab

nextRevision.basis: Until 2025 Punjab adjusted its rates with the consumer price index twice a year, from 1 March and 1 September (the department's own compilation of adjustments, 1995 to 2025). The 1 May 2026 notification under the Code on Wages resets the base rates and leaves later adjustments to 'such intervals and in such manner as prescribed by the Punjab Government' (note 10); the Code on Wages (Punjab) Rules, 2026 were still a draft when checked. 1 March 2027 is the next date on the old cycle; no adjustment from 1 September 2026 was listed on the department's site on 17 October 2026.

verification: 2026-10-17: pblabour.gov.in home page (the department's notifications block; /Profile/Notification renders its list by script and shows no documents to a plain fetch) links 'Notification on No. Labour-Lab0MIWA/1/2021-4L (260032)/166.-In Dated 1st MAY,2026 Notification Regarding Bye Basic Minimum rates of wages w.e.f 1st May 2026', the brick-kiln piece rates from the same date, and the 1995-2025 compilation. No later wage notification or adjustment was listed.

2026-10-17: 8ec9bd9d..._Basic Minimum rates of wages.pdf, Punjab Government Gazette (Extraordinary), 1 May 2026, 3 pages, Code on Wages s. 8(3), signed Manvesh Singh Sidhu, Secretary, Labour. The rate tables are images; read at 260 dpi. Per month / per day / per hour: unskilled 13486 / 518.69 / 64.83; semi-skilled 14383 / 553.19 / 69.14; skilled 15414 / 592.84 / 74.10; highly skilled 16601 / 638.50 / 79.81. Staff Category A 19431 / 747.34 / 93.41; B 17510 / 673.46 / 84.18; C 15786 / 607.15 / 75.89; D 14406 / 554.07 / 69.25. Attached agricultural labour 90973.28 a year with meals; other agricultural labour 486.588 a day with meals, 540.983 without.

2026-10-17: Notes in the notification: rates are basic rates that may not be split into allowances (1, 9); full neutralisation of CPI movement, adjustment as prescribed under the Code (1, 10); daily rate is the monthly rate / 26 and includes the weekly rest day, but a day's deduction for absence is monthly / 30 (7, 16); the principal employer is responsible for contractors paying these rates (5, 11); 30% / 10% less in hotels, restaurants, tea stalls, halwais, ahatas and households where meals and lodging are given (13); 8-hour normal day (15).

2026-10-17: The notification's daily figures are the monthly rate / 26, mostly rounded to the nearest paisa, but skilled 15414 / 26 = 592.846 is printed 592.84 (truncated). The printed figures are used ('stated').

2026-10-17: Minimum wages rates w.e.f. 1.7.1995 to 1.9.2025-2-1.pdf (112 scanned pages, Punjabi headings, no text layer), page 108 (table 1): from 01.03.2025 unskilled 11389.64 / 438.06 / 54.75, semi-skilled 12169.64 / 468.06 / 58.50, skilled 13066.64 / 502.56 / 62.82, highly skilled 14098.64 / 542.25 / 67.78; from 01.09.2025 11726.40 / 451.01 / 56.37, 12506.40 / 481.01 / 60.12, 13403.40 / 515.51 / 64.43, 14435.40 / 555.20 / 69.40. Read at 150 dpi; the scan is faint, a reviewer should confirm. The compilation has no single number or date; the date given here is its last adjustment.

OPEN QUESTION for the reviewer: when the next adjustment falls. The old cycle was 1 March and 1 September; the 2026 notification leaves the interval to rules, and the Code on Wages (Punjab) Rules, 2026 were published only in draft (29 December 2025, per secondary reports). The Central rules use 1 April and 1 October. nextRevision is set to 1 March 2027 without marking 1 September 2026 as missed.
NOT INCLUDED: Staff Categories A to D (no matching skill labels on the site yet), agricultural labour, and brick kilns (separate piece-rate notification).

2026-10-17: Staff categories A to D read from the 'Staff wise Categories' table (Gazette p. 2212) and definitions (pp. 2212-2213): A 19,431 / 747.34; B 17,510 / 673.46; C 15,786 / 607.15; D 14,406 / 554.07 a month / a day. They sit alongside the four skill levels and apply in all establishments. Category D covers 'any Class-IV employee (casual, through contractor or on contract basis)', ₹920 a month above unskilled.

2026-10-17: Labour Welfare Fund amounts. Punjab Act 32 of 2014 (Gazette Extra 15 Dec 2014; Bill 1 of 2014 on punjabassembly.gov.in) set ₹5 worker and ₹20 employer a month. The Vidhan Sabha passed the Punjab Labour Welfare Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2025 on 11 July 2025 to double them to ₹10 and ₹40 (news reports only); no assent, Act number or Gazette notice found on 17 October 2026. The page shows the 2014 amounts and says so.

2026-10-17: the 1 May 2026 notification fixes rates 'in respect of all employments in the State of Punjab' (establishments, factories, employees, workers and contract labour under the Code on Wages) and lists none; note 14 places anyone not named in the category they most accurately fit. Its exceptions: agricultural labour (gazette page 2213, tables are images, re-read at 400 dpi: attached labour in agriculture, unskilled, consolidated per annum with meals or food grains, 90973.28 a year; other agriculture labour 486.588 a day with meals, 540.983 without), brick kilns ('will be notified separately'), and note 13: in hotels, restaurants, tea stalls, halwais, ahatas and taverns attached to wine and liquor shops, and for domestic workers, the minimum is 30 per cent less where two meals, tea twice and lodging are given, and 10 per cent less with two meals and tea twice but no lodging.

2026-10-17: brick-kiln notification /209 of 25 May 2026 (2 pages, text layer, page 1 checked by eye), effective 1 May 2026, per 1000 bricks or tiles: pathera with jamadari commission 1112 bricks, 1238 tiles; without 1047 and 1178; bharaiwala, animal driven, 414 up to 400 m plus 31 for each further 100 m or part; bharaiwala, tempo or truck, 360 up to 1000 m plus 25 for each further 400 m or part; truck trolley loading and unloading (pucca bricks) 307; chennai wala 84; keri wala 70; nikasi wala 265; mistri 206 per 1000 bricks burnt by a batch of four, the mistri getting 112 a day more than the rest. No DA or CPI link stated ('subject to revision as per the provisions of the Code on Wages'). The home page lists it under the number /166 by mistake; the document prints /209.
